newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Govt details health, education, police funding.
newsitem.headline: NZ Govt details health, education, police funding.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters on Thursday announced that the government's 1997/98 budget allocated an extra NZ$300 million to health in 1997/98 and in each of the following two years.
On top of that NZ$900 million, the government planned to provide a further $180 million per year in the 1998 budget, rising to $450 million in the 1999 budget.
"This will mean that, for the first time, health managers will have the opportunity to plan ahead on the basis of realistic expectations of futures funding levels," Peters said.

He said the extra $300 million per year contained in the 1997/98 budget would provide extra resources for elective surgery to reduce waiting lists, free doctor visits and pharmaceuticals for all children under six, and better mental health services.
Peters said the government would allocate between $150 and $200 million over the next three years to assist students with special needs.
In the drive to ensure safer communities, the budget allocated further funding to allow 200 additional police recruits who would be trained by June 30, 1998.
